title: Strict-henselian fraction field and the residue inertia kernel
statement:
Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] with residue field $\kappa$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Let $H=A^{\mathrm h}$ be its henselization (the universal local henselian extension with unchanged residue field, where henselian is as in [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]) and let $R=A^{\mathrm{sh}}$ be its strict henselization at a geometric closed point, as in [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit] applied to $\operatorname{Spec}A$. Choose a separable closure $\kappa^{\mathrm{sep}}$ of $\kappa$ and a compatible separable closure $\Omega$ of $K=\operatorname{Frac}(H)$ [def-pd-separable-closure]. The rings $H$ and $R$ are domains, and one can embed $H\subset R\subset\Omega$ compatibly with the chosen residue identification $R/\mathfrak m_R\simeq\kappa^{\mathrm{sep}}$. Put $L=\operatorname{Frac}(R)\subset\Omega$. The residue homomorphism
$$
\mathrm{res}:G=\operatorname{Gal}(\Omega/K)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Gal}(\kappa^{\mathrm{sep}}/\kappa)
$$
is surjective, and, writing $I=\ker(\mathrm{res})$, one has
$$
L=\Omega^I,\qquad I=\operatorname{Gal}(\Omega/L).
$$
Here $\Omega^I$ is the subfield fixed by every element of $I$, and $\Omega$ is also a separable closure of $L$; thus $I$ is the absolute Galois group of $L$, with its Krull topology. The extension $L/K$ is Galois and restriction and reduction induce isomorphisms
$$
G/I\simeq\operatorname{Gal}(L/K)\simeq\operatorname{Aut}_H(R)\simeq\operatorname{Gal}(\kappa^{\mathrm{sep}}/\kappa).
$$
Every $\sigma\in G$ preserves $R\subset\Omega$, and its induced automorphism of $R$ has residue action $\mathrm{res}(\sigma)$.

source.place: Tag 0BSW (lemma-identify-inertia), with its setup in Section Tag 0BSD (section-ramification): K^h and K^sh are the henselian and strict-henselian fraction fields; the proof identifies K^sh with the inertia fixed field and Aut(A^sh/A^h) with the residue Galois group.

proof.text: A DVR is a valuation ring by the equivalence explicitly included in [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]; hence [lem-weil-pbc-valuation-ring-normal] makes $A$ a normal domain. By [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-normal-iff-integrally-closed-total-fractions], $A$ is also a normal ring: a domain is reduced, has the single minimal prime $(0)$, and its total ring of fractions is its fraction field. Apply [lem-trf-henselization-prime-ind-etale] at the maximal ideal, using $A_{\mathfrak m_A}=A$ and the universal-property convention [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime]. Thus $H$ is ind-etale, that is, a filtered colimit of etale $A$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. It is local by the henselization setup. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-etale-colimit-normal-local-domain] gives that $H$ is a normal domain and $A\to H$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 0BSD (section-ramification), normality of the henselization; algebra.tex Tags 00PD, 00IC and 04GN; more-algebra.tex Tag 06DI; algebra.tex Tag 030C (lemma-characterize-reduced-ring-normal), (2) implies (1), specialized to a domain

proof.text: By [lem-wf-strict-henselization-finite-lifts], $R$ is the local colimit of the finite local etale $H$-algebras $B_e$ indexed by finite Galois subextensions $e/\kappa$ in $\kappa^{\mathrm{sep}}$, with residue field $\kappa^{\mathrm{sep}}$. The conclusion of this comparison includes the pointed-neighbourhood convention of the item as well as the ring-theoretic construction. In particular this is a comparison of actual colimits over $A$ and $H$, not an inference from the definition of finite-etale reduction. The normal domain $H$ is also a normal ring by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-normal-iff-integrally-closed-total-fractions], again using that a domain is reduced with the single minimal prime $(0)$ and has total ring of fractions equal to its fraction field. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-etale-colimit-normal-local-domain] over $H$ gives that $R$ is a normal domain and $H\to R$ is injective. For every $e$, [lem-wf-henselian-finite-galois-lift] supplies the normal domain $B_e$, the finite Galois field $E_e=K\otimes_HB_e=\operatorname{Frac}(B_e)$, and its integral-closure description.

source.place: Tag 0BSW (lemma-identify-inertia), finite-etale-lift paragraph; algebra.tex Tag 0BSL (remark-construct-sh-from-h); more-algebra.tex Tag 06DI; algebra.tex Tag 030C (lemma-characterize-reduced-ring-normal), (2) implies (1), specialized to a domain

proof.text: The map $B_e\to R$ is injective: after inverting the nonzero elements of $H$ it gives a unital map from the field $E_e$ to the field $\operatorname{Frac}(R)$, hence is injective, and $B_e\subset E_e$. Every fraction of elements of $R$ is represented by two elements at a common finite stage, so $L=\operatorname{Frac}(R)=\bigcup_e E_e$. In particular $L/K$ is separable algebraic. Each $K$-minimal polynomial of an element of $L$ is separable and splits in the chosen separable closure $\Omega$, by [lem-weil-pbc-separable-closure-exists-galois] and [def-pd-separable-closure]. Apply [lem-exc-etale-embedding-extension-sepclosed] with base $K$, extension field $L$, starting intermediate field $K$, and target $\Omega$. Its integrality and splitting hypotheses have just been verified. This embeds $L$ into $\Omega$, and hence embeds $H\subset R\subset\Omega$. The residue identification remains the specified one on the abstract $R$ under this embedding.

source.place: Tag 0BSD, compatible embedding into a separable closure; Tag 0BSW, the finite lifts and their fraction fields

proof.text: Let $\sigma\in G$. Each embedded $E_e/K$ is finite Galois, so $\sigma(E_e)=E_e$. By the integral-closure assertion of [lem-wf-henselian-finite-galois-lift], its subring $B_e$ is preserved: a monic relation over $H$ remains such after applying $\sigma$ or $\sigma^{-1}$. Thus $\sigma(R)=R$ and $\sigma(L)=L$. An automorphism of the local ring $R$ preserves its unique maximal ideal, so it induces a residue automorphism fixing $\kappa$. Define $\mathrm{res}(\sigma)(\bar r)=\overline{\sigma(r)}$ under $R/\mathfrak m_R=\kappa^{\mathrm{sep}}$. This is well defined and respects composition because reduction does, giving the residue homomorphism in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0BSW, preservation and residue action; normality and finite-stage integral-closure calculation

proof.text: Let $\tau\in\operatorname{Gal}(\kappa^{\mathrm{sep}}/\kappa)$. Each finite Galois residue subfield $e$ is preserved by $\tau$. Full faithfulness in [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-finite-etale-equivalence] gives a unique $H$-automorphism $t_e$ of $B_e$ reducing to $\tau|_e$. For $e\subset f$, the composites $B_e\to B_f$ obtained by first $t_e$ or last $t_f$ have the same residue map $\tau|_e:e\to f$, so full faithfulness makes them equal. They induce an automorphism $t$ of $R$, with inverse built from $\tau^{-1}$, and an automorphism $t_L$ of $L$ over $K$. To extend $t_L$ to $\Omega$, use [lem-exc-etale-embedding-extension-sepclosed] with base $K$, extension $\Omega$, intermediate field $L$ and target $\Omega$. By [lem-weil-pbc-separable-closure-exists-galois], every element is algebraic and every $K$-minimal polynomial splits there. The resulting $K$-embedding $u:\Omega\to\Omega$ is onto: for any $a\in\Omega$, $u$ injects the finite set of roots in $\Omega$ of its $K$-minimal polynomial into itself, hence permutes that set, so $a$ is in its image. Thus $u\in G$, with residue $\tau$, proving surjectivity of $\mathrm{res}$.

source.place: Tag 0BSW, the finite Galois residue lifts and surjectivity; finite-stage maps are lifted using algebra.tex Tag 04GK

proof.text: If $\sigma\in I=\ker(\mathrm{res})$, Step 4 makes its restriction to every $B_e$ an $H$-automorphism with identity reduction on $e$. Full faithfulness in [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-finite-etale-equivalence] forces that restriction to be the identity. Thus $\sigma$ fixes $R$ and its fraction field $L$. Conversely, an element of $G$ fixing $L$ fixes $R$, hence its entire residue field $\kappa^{\mathrm{sep}}$, and belongs to $I$. This proves $I=\operatorname{Gal}(\Omega/L)$.

source.place: Tag 0BSW, kernel of the residue action

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-separable-closure-exists-galois], $\Omega/K$ is Galois and for the intermediate field $L$, $\Omega/L$ is separable algebraic and normal. The fixed-field theorem [lem-exc-etale-galois-fixed-field-subgroup] applied to the subgroup fixing $L$, identified with $I$ in Step 6, gives $\Omega^I=L$. The field $\Omega$ is separably closed by [def-pd-separable-closure], and separable algebraic over $L$, so it is a separable closure of $L$. Explicitly, the $L$-minimal polynomial of any $a\in\Omega$ divides its separable $K$-minimal polynomial in $L[T]$; it is therefore separable. This does not treat an arbitrary polynomial in $L[T]$ as a polynomial in $K[T]$. Thus the equality in Step 6 identifies $I$ with the absolute Galois group of $L$.

source.place: Tag 0BSW, fixed field and absolute Galois group of the strict-henselian fraction field

proof.text: This identification respects the Krull topologies. By definition a neighbourhood basis of the identity in the automorphism group of an algebraic extension is given by pointwise stabilizers of finite subsets of the extension field. For a finite subset $S\subset\Omega$, the subgroup fixing $S$ in $\operatorname{Gal}(\Omega/L)$ is exactly $I\cap\{\sigma\in G:\sigma|_S=\mathrm{id}\}$. Both Krull neighbourhood bases are therefore the same after intersection with $I$. No finiteness hypothesis on $L/K$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 0BSW, profinite subgroup identification; elementary comparison of the defining finite-subset stabilizer bases

proof.text: Every $K$-embedding $v:L\to\Omega$ extends to a $K$-embedding $\Omega\to\Omega$ by [lem-exc-etale-embedding-extension-sepclosed], with the splitting hypotheses as in Step 5. The finite-root-set argument there makes the extension an element of $G$, so Step 4 gives $v(L)=L$. This proves normality explicitly: if $a\in L$ and $b\in\Omega$ is any root of its irreducible polynomial over $K$, the isomorphism $K(a)\to K(b)$ sending $a$ to $b$ extends to an element of $G$ by the same lemma; hence $b\in L$. Those polynomials split in $\Omega$ by [lem-weil-pbc-separable-closure-exists-galois], so they split in $L$. Since Step 3 already established separability and algebraicity, $L/K$ is Galois. In particular every $K$-automorphism of $L$ extends to $G$ and consequently preserves $R$.

source.place: Tag 0BSW, normality of the strict-henselian fraction extension and extension of its automorphisms

proof.text: Extension to fractions injects $\operatorname{Aut}_H(R)$ into $\operatorname{Gal}(L/K)$; conversely every $K$-automorphism of $L$ preserves $R$ by Step 9, so restriction is its inverse. The map $G\to\operatorname{Gal}(L/K)$ is onto by Step 9 and has kernel $I$ by Step 6; explicitly $\sigma I\mapsto\sigma|_L$ is a bijective homomorphism. Reduction $\operatorname{Aut}_H(R)\to\operatorname{Gal}(\kappa^{\mathrm{sep}}/\kappa)$ is onto by Step 5. If an automorphism of $R$ has trivial reduction, extend it to $L$ and then to $G$ as in Step 9; the extension belongs to $I$ and fixes $L$ by Step 6, so the original automorphism is the identity. Thus reduction is also injective. These maps give precisely all three displayed isomorphisms. Step 4 already proves the final preservation and residue-action formula for every $\sigma\in G$.

source.place: Tag 0BSW, final automorphism/residue identifications; elementary fractions and explicit quotient bijection using Steps 4-6 and 9
